body.hook: Does listening to music while studying help or hurt? You could ask your friends, survey your class or run an experiment. Each method gives a different kind of answer, and only one can show cause and effect.

study.title: Choosing the Right Method
study.question: How do psychologists answer research questions?
study.passage:
Research methods:
• Experiment: change the independent variable, measure the dependent variable, control everything else. The only method that can show cause and effect.
• Correlational study: measure two variables and see if they're related. Correlation does not mean causation.
• Survey: ask many people questions; useful for opinions and habits, but people may not answer honestly or accurately.
• Case study: study one person in depth; rich detail, but results may not apply to others.
• Naturalistic observation: watch behaviour in real settings without interfering.
Example of correlation vs causation: Ice cream sales and drowning rates are positively correlated. Does ice cream cause drowning? No: a third variable, hot weather, increases both.
Research questions (groups choose the best method and explain):
1. Does background music affect memory for a word list?
2. Is screen time related to sleep hours in Grade 11 students?
3. How do students feel about a later school start time?
4. How did one person recover language after a brain injury?
Mini-experiment: Test question 1 in class with two groups (music vs silence), each memorizing 20 words for 2 minutes, then recalling them. Record results and identify possible confounding variables.
